scenes.body: We make Lynkk. We'll tell you where another tool is the better pick.
vo: We ran the same sales call through six AI note takers and scored them on five things that matter after the call ends.
The winner depends on one question: what do you do with your notes next?
In the next few minutes: how each one captures your call, where the summaries actually differ, and at the end, exactly which tool we'd pick for which kind of work.
Welcome to the Lynkk channel.
Quick disclosure: we make one of these six tools.
So we'll show you our scoring, and we'll tell you where another tool is the better pick.
The six are Otter, Fireflies, Fathom, Granola, Read AI and Lynkk.
Same recorded discovery call, scored on capture, summary quality, follow-up, memory across calls, and price.

head: Three ways to capture.
Bot, no bot, in the room.
vo: First, capture.
There are three ways these tools get your audio.
One: a bot joins the call as a participant.
That's how Otter, Fireflies and Fathom usually work.
It's reliable, but everyone sees "Notetaker has joined."
Two: no bot.
The tool records from your own computer, the way Granola does.
Three: in the room, for meetings that don't have a video link at all.
Lynkk covers all three: a meeting bot if you want one, a Chrome extension or Mac app if you don't, and in-room recording.

head: Every tool summarizes.
The details decide.
vo: Summary quality.
Every tool gave us a usable summary.
The differences were in the details.
Did it catch the budget?
The decision maker?
The next step, with a date?
Fireflies is the one reviewers usually single out for summaries and action items, so if a clean auto-summary is all you need, start there.

head: Notes don't close deals.
Follow-ups do.
scenes.body: Lynkk drafts it from the call. You review and send it.
vo: Follow-ups and tasks.
This is where most notes go to die.
A summary is nice, but the deal moves when the follow-up goes out.
Lynkk drafts the follow-up email from what was actually said, and you review and send it.
It never sends on its own.
Action items come out as tasks with owners and due dates, on a Kanban board.

head: Most tools forget.
Lynkk remembers.
scenes.body: No CRM sync yet. Copy the brief into Salesforce or HubSpot.
vo: Memory across calls.
Most tools treat every meeting as a separate file.
Lynkk groups every call with the same account into one history, and tracks budget, stakeholders and objections over time.
On Pro, you can ask a question across all those calls and get the answer with its source.
One honest gap: Lynkk doesn't sync to your CRM yet.
You copy the brief into Salesforce or HubSpot.
If automatic CRM sync is a must-have today, factor that in.

head: Free plans differ.
Here's the fine print.

vo: Pricing.
Fathom's free plan is the one reviewers call most generous.
Otter's free plan has a monthly minutes cap.
Granola's free tier covers a limited number of meetings.
Lynkk's free plan gives you unlimited notes up to two hours each, plus your first five hours of AI summaries, no credit card.
Pro is fifteen dollars a month, or $9.75 a month billed yearly.

head: Who should pick which?

cells: Your own typed notes, cleaned up
Strong summaries for a whole team

vo: So who should pick which?
If you want the most generous free recording, look at Fathom.
If you like typing your own notes and want them cleaned up, Granola.
Rolling out to a whole team and mainly want strong summaries? Fireflies.
Already living in Otter for mobile and in-person transcription? Otter's fine.
Meeting analytics? Read AI.
And if you sell for a living and need every call with an account remembered, with the follow-up already drafted, that's exactly what we built Lynkk for.
